main_body: A small wooden cradle: a tall headboard at the left, a tan rim, a cream pillow and a light-blue blanket inside, and short dark legs below.
top_band: In the middle column (x≈8) the tan rim covers rows 3-4 (about 2px), then dark brown interior at rows 4-6 and the cream pillow at rows 6-8. A second tan band at rows 9-10 is the front rim, with dark legs below.
evidence: The cradle reads as an end-on profile. The headboard and footboard are vertical slabs, and the only wood bands are thin 2-3 row rims. The interior is shown as a stack of vertical faces (back panel, pillow, blanket) and not as a foreshortened horizontal surface. There is no clear lit top band with a front edge line and eave shadow above a distinct front face. The legs are tiny, so the front face is only about 3px tall. It matches the side-elevation and rim-only failure patterns in the guide.

style.evidence: The wood has only about 3 tones (tan, mid brown, dark brown), where the stall and well references have 5-6 steps per material. The pillow and blanket are small flat patches with minimal highlights. The surfaces have no grain or texture dots. The outline is a dark brown/grey lean that is partly near-black against the background. Most tiles use only a handful of colours, well below the reference tiles.
